newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Almazy Rossii-Sakha sees $350 mln Eurobond in '97.
newsitem.headline: Almazy Rossii-Sakha sees $350 mln Eurobond in '97.

text.p: Russian gem group Almazy Rossii-Sakha plans to issue a $350 million Eurobond with a 3-5 year maturity, hopefully by year end, vice president for finance Viktor Sofronov said on Tuesday.

"Three hundred and fifty million is the preliminary figure, but it could be changed," he told Reuters, adding that the group, Russia's near-monopoly diamond producer, had chosen SBC Warburg and Smith Barney to lead manage the issue.

The company, known as ALROSA and previously as ARS, had earlier planned to issue a bond worth $100 million. When asked if the $350 million bond would be issued in tranches, Sofronov said "no, it will probably be all at once...optimistically, it will be by the end of the year."
ALROSA also said it was finishing negotiations for a short-term syndicated loan of up to $50 million through Britain's Singer & Friendlander to be backed by diamond sales to Russian polishers.
Moscow has granted ALROSA a diamond export license but still has not approved a gem export agreement with South Africa's De Beers. ALROSA is De Beers' trade and negotiating partner.
The agreement has been awaiting final government approval for months and repeated official predictions of a quick resolution have not materialised.
